successors.name: Duchy of Bavaria
successors.text: Upper Bavaria with the Palatinate and Nordgau, seated at Munich; Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria row begins in 1260

successors.name: Duchy of Lower Bavaria (House of Wittelsbach)
successors.text: Lower Bavaria, seated at Landshut and Burghausen

ledger.x: 907: Arnulf the Bad becomes duke of Bavaria after his father Luitpold falls at Pressburg.
911: Arnulf unites Bavaria and Carinthia.
916: Conrad I invades Bavaria.
919: Arnulf returns to Bavaria.
921: Henry the Fowler marches on Bavaria.
921: Arnulf recognises Henry's sovereignty and keeps Bavaria.
938: King Otto I deposes Duke Eberhard and Berthold succeeds his brother.
948: Otto I installs his brother Henry I as duke of Bavaria; the Ottonian house now holds the duchy.
952: Henry I receives the Italian March of Verona.

c. 960: Otto I sets up the Eastern March (Ostarrichi) below the Enns as a Bavarian march. 'by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave'; the Lechfeld victory of 955 had begun the reconquest; the page calls it the Bavarian Eastern March. eu-08-a's Kingdom of Germany…
Before 970: the March of Styria exists as a march of Bavaria.
976: Otto II cuts the Duchy of Carinthia out of Bavaria.
976: the March of Verona goes with Carinthia.
976: the march leaves Bavaria.
1061: Agnes of Poitou enfeoffs Otto of Nordheim with the duchy; the Salian regency replaces the Ottonians' line.
1070: Henry IV establishes Welf rule over Bavaria; the Welf dukes hold it, with breaks, to 1180.
1139: Leopold IV, a Babenberg, is given Bavaria after Henry the Proud is dispossessed in 1138.
1156: Austria is raised to a duchy independent of Bavaria.
1156: Henry the Lion regains Bavaria as a 'diminished' duchy when the Babenbergs renounce it at the Regensburg diet of 8 September 1156.
1180: Otto of Wittelsbach becomes duke of Bavaria.
1213: the archbishop of Salzburg becomes a prince of the Empire.
1255: Bavaria is partitioned into Upper Bavaria (Munich, with the Palatinate and Nordgau) and Lower Bavaria (Landshut and Burghausen).

wars.name: Conrad I's war against Arnulf of Bavaria
wars.outcome: Conrad's forces invaded Bavaria in 916 and drove Arnulf into exile in Hungary; Conrad's death in 918/919 let Arnulf return and expel the king's forces.

wars.name: Henry the Fowler's campaigns against Arnulf
wars.outcome: Henry defeated Arnulf in two campaigns in 921; Arnulf recognised Henry's sovereignty and kept autonomous rule over Bavaria.

wars.name: Luitpolding revolt
wars.outcome: The Luitpolding attempt to regain power in 954 was crushed.

wars.name: Battle of Lechfeld
wars.outcome: Otto I's victory at the Battle of Lechfeld in 955 ended the Hungarian threat and began the reconquest of the Danube lands below the Enns.

wars.name: War of the Three Henries
wars.outcome: Henry II revolted against Otto II in 974 and was deposed in 976; Otto II split Carinthia from Bavaria.

wars.name: Babenberg-Welf dispute over Bavaria
wars.outcome: Henry the Proud was dispossessed in 1138; Bavaria went to Leopold IV in 1139 and Henry Jasomirgott in 1141; at the Regensburg diet of 8 September 1156 the Babenbergs renounced it and Austria became a duchy by the Privilegium Minus of 17 September 1156.

wars.name: Fall of Henry the Lion
wars.outcome: Henry the Lion was banned in 1180; Otto of Wittelsbach received Bavaria on 16 September 1180 and Styria was separated.

certainty.note: No treaty defines the stem duchy's borders on the pages opened; the Privilegium Minus of 1156 names no counties, so the Austrian frontier is a reading of the Enns line.
